chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Al-Husayn ibn Hashim from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And if a woman fears from her husband cruelty or desertion'.

He said: This is when the woman is with him, and he does not find her pleasing, so he desires to divorce her. So she says to him, 'Keep me and do not divorce me, and I will leave for you what is upon your back (the dower), and give you from my wealth, and free you from my day and my night,' so all that is agreeable to him.

key_terms.أُحَلِّلَكَ: I free you / I make permissible for you
key_terms.مَا عَلَى ظَهْرِكَ: What is upon your back (referring to the dower/mahr)
key_terms.نُشُوزاً: Cruelity or deviation by the husband

ai.seo_question: What does the Imam say about the meaning of a woman fearing her husband's cruelty or desertion in Surah An-Nisa?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the mechanism of *Khul'* (redemption) by explaining that the verse addresses a scenario where a husband, dissatisfied with his wife, seeks divorce. The wife proactively offers financial concessions—such as retaining the dower or granting him freedom from marital duties—to secure her position, a mutual agreement the husband accepts willingly. This hadith provides the foundational Shia jurisprudential understanding of *Khul'* as a consensual dissolution initiated by the wife's offer, distinct from *Talaq* (husband-initiated divorce).

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from Al Husayn Bin Hashim, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I asked himasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [4:128] And if a woman fears from her husband, either cruelty or desertion.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is where the woman happens to be with him who does not get attracted her, so he wants to divorce her. So she is saying to him, ‘Keep me and do not divorce me, and I will leave for you what is upon your back (dower), and give you from my wealth, and free you from my day and my night’, so all that is agreeable to him’.
en.sarwar: 3. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from ibn Sama‘ah from al-Husayn ibn Hashim from abu Basir who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, ‘If a woman is afraid of disharmony from her husband or his disregarding her. . . .’ [4:128]

He (the Imam) said, ‘This is a man who has a wife whom he does not like. He wants to divorce her, thus, she says to him, “Keep me and do not divorce me. I will leave for you what you owe to me and pay you from my assets, wave in your favor my day and night,” all such offers are acceptable for him.’”
